title: Native coefficient hearts and normalized open/proper forgetting
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ and let $g_T$ be geometric Galois Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $R_T$ on the small pro-etale site be the sheaf of continuous $\Omega$-valued functions taking values locally in a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Put $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $P_T=g_T^*$, $\mathcal B_T=\mathcal A_T^{P_T}$, whose objects are $(M,\theta:P_TM\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$ and arrows intertwine $\theta$ [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Write $U_T$ for the forgetful functor and also its termwise derived functor on ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal C_T\subset D(\mathcal A_T)$ for objects with bounded cohomology admitting a finite locally closed stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions, and $\mathcal W(T_0)=U_T^{-1}(\mathcal C_T)\subset D(\mathcal B_T)$, with full subcategory morphisms. These are the actual native categories of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with geometric fiber $f:X\to Y$. Choose the native compactification $f_0=p_0j_0$ and its geometric fiber $f=pj$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

The coefficient ring $B_{T_0}$ of locally finite-dimensional-span functions in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] is canonically $R_T$, respecting restrictions, multiplication and finite-extension inclusions; its internal module objects identify with sectionwise $R_T$-module sheaves with identical actions. The categories $\mathcal A_T$ and $\mathcal B_T$ are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Site reindexing by $g_T$ and $g_T^{-1}$ gives inverse exact coefficient-preserving equivalences $P_T$ and $P_T^{-1}$. The functor $U_T$ is exact and conservative, has the exact free-action left adjoint with underlying object $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}P_T^nM$, preserves K-injective complexes [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], and $D(U_T)$ is conservative, commutes with cohomology and shifts, and preserves cone triangles. Thus boundedness and the stated constructibility are tested after forgetting.

Open extension by zero is exact and its native lift forgets to ordinary $j_!$. For proper pushforward let $a:P_Yp_*\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*P_{\overline X}$ be the native Frobenius comparison, so its fixed-pair lift is $(M,\theta)\mapsto(p_*M,p_*(\theta)a_M)$. Put $F^{\mathrm W}=Rp_*^{\mathrm W}j_!^{\mathrm W}$ on ordinary native derived categories and $F^c=Rp_*j_!$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$c^0:U_YF^{\mathrm W}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^cU_X.$$
Its proper factor is the total-right-derived comparison induced by the equality on sheaf functors, including their derived-unit maps. On a native K-injective resolution $I$ after open extension it is the identity of $Q(p_*U_{\overline X}I)$, where $Q$ is localization; on that representative both Frobenius maps are $Q(p_*(\theta_I)a_{UI})$. Consequently $c^0$ respects the induced Frobenius actions, shifts and all localized derived morphisms. It compares the actual ordered open/proper constructions; it assumes no exceptional adjoint.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-locally-finite-coefficient-ring-realization] on each geometric fibre $T$. Its coefficient isomorphism identifies the finite-extension coefficient sheaf $R_T$ with the native $B_{T_0}$, and its naturality square identifies restriction and geometric coefficient maps. In particular multiplication and the inclusions of finite coefficient fields agree, not merely the underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Native coefficient identification preceding the Frobenius-equivariance construction; the existing coefficient-realization lemma supplies the function-sheaf comparison.

proof.text: Unpack an internal $B$-module action in sheaves of $\underline\Omega$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], a map $B\otimes_{\underline\Omega}M\to M$ is exactly a restriction-compatible family of $\underline\Omega(V)$-balanced bilinear maps $B(V)\times M(V)\to M(V)$. The unit and associativity diagrams say $1m=m$ and $(bb')m=b(b'm)$ on sections. Conversely a sectionwise $B(V)$-module action supplies these maps, after restricting scalars along $\underline\Omega\to B$. The two assignments are inverse; the morphism condition in the same definition is precisely sectionwise $B(V)$-linearity. Hence the module presentations, actions and forgetful functors agree.

source.place: Tensor product, label section-tensor-product (03EK), and sheafification, label lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules (03CY); direct unpacking of the module-object axioms.

proof.text: Use the small site models of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. The sheaf $R_T$ is commutative, so [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] applies and makes $\mathcal A_T$ Grothendieck abelian. Apply the site-reindexing assertion of [lem-sf-weil-frobenius-action-resolutions]: postcomposition by $g_T$ and $g_T^{-1}$ preserves coverings, gives inverse site equivalences and identifies the coefficient functions with the same functions, retaining their finite coefficient fields. Thus the module functors $P_T$ and $P_T^{-1}$ are inverse additive exact equivalences, with the native coefficient actions.

source.place: frobeniusPullback and ProEtaleWeilSheaf; site and ringed-module assertions supplied by the explicitly cited nodes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-fixed-pair-derived-forget-comparison] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal A_T$ and $F=P_T$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 3. It gives Grothendieck abelianness of $\mathcal B_T$, exact conservative $U_T$, the exact free-action left adjoint $M\mapsto\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}P_T^nM$ with shifting structure, preservation of K-injectives and conservativity of $D(U_T)$. Exactness gives $U_T\ker d=\ker(U_Td)$ and preserves images and their quotients, so $H^a(D(U_T)K)=U_TH^a(K)$ naturally. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], $D(U_T)$ also commutes with shifts and takes cone triangles to distinguished triangles. Since $U_T$ reflects zero objects, vanishing in each degree, hence boundedness, is tested after forgetting.

source.place: Free.preservesHomology_functor, preservesKInjectiveComplexes_forget; derived conservativity in IsoAlgebraComp.lean; termwise exactness for cohomology and triangles.

proof.text: The geometric fibres are separated finite-type $k$-schemes by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Finite type gives quasi-compactness; separatedness gives quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus [lem-sf-native-adic-qcqs-stratification] identifies the local constructibility condition of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] with a finite stratification of the whole fibre by locally closed constructible subschemes with lisse restrictions. The converse restricts such a partition to open subsets; the strata stay constructible because $T$, of finite type over $k$, is a Noetherian space, where every finite union of locally closed subsets is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Step 2 identifies the restricted rings and finite free modules. Together with Step 4's cohomology identity, this proves that the displayed $\mathcal W(T_0)=U_T^{-1}(\mathcal C_T)$ is exactly the native bounded constructible full subcategory, and proves constructibility is tested after forgetting.

By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] the pro-etale site of the open $X$ is the localization of that of $\overline X$ at $X$. On an object over $X$, both restricted coefficient sheaves are the identical locally finite functions. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to this ringed localization: the ordinary $j_!$ is exact. The actual native lift is specified in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] as $(M,\theta)\mapsto(j_!M,j_!(\theta)c_M)$, hence $U_{\overline X}j_!^{\mathrm W}=j_!U_X$ on sheaves and their maps. The lift is exact as well: its underlying short sequences are exact by ordinary $j_!$, and the exact conservative forgetful functor tests exactness by its cohomology identity. Termwise application therefore gives the same equality after localization, by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated].

source.place: Labels lemma-extension-by-zero and lemma-extension-by-zero-exact (03DI,03DJ), applied through the cited ringed-localization statements.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-compactification-middle-over-base] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$) the compactification $\overline X_0$ is separated of finite type over $k_0$, so Steps 3--5 apply to $T_0=\overline X_0$ and to $T_0=Y_0$. The ordinary module $p_*$ is additive and left exact: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] makes it a right adjoint, and a compatible family of maps into a limit corresponds under its Hom adjunction to a compatible family into the original limit. The native proper lift is the lift for $L=p_*$ and $e=a$ in [lem-sf-fixed-pair-derived-forget-comparison], by the formula in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Applying that lemma with $(\mathcal C,F)=(\mathcal A_{\overline X},P_{\overline X})$ and $(\mathcal D,H)=(\mathcal A_Y,P_Y)$ gives Grothendieck hearts, K-injective preservation by $U_{\overline X}$ and a derived isomorphism $U_YRp_*^{\mathrm W}\cong Rp_*U_{\overline X}$. The lift formula gives the literal equality $U_Yp_*^{\mathrm W}=p_*U_{\overline X}$ on objects and morphisms; Step 8 takes the comparison $d$ induced by this equality and normalized by the units on all K-injective complexes, rather than an independently chosen objectwise isomorphism.

source.place: rightDerivedFunctorMapOfNatIsoCompForgetIso, canonical comparison of the two total right derived functors.

proof.text: For a complex $K$ in the native source, take a K-injective resolution $s:j_!^{\mathrm W}K\to I$ in $\mathcal B_{\overline X}$ by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. Step 4 makes $U_{\overline X}I$ K-injective and $U_{\overline X}s$ a quasi-isomorphism. The K-injective computation and unit normalization in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] identify both sides of $d$ with $Q(p_*U_{\overline X}I)$; the normalization follows from the units themselves. At $I$, write $\eta_I^{\mathrm W}$ and $\eta_{UI}$ for the native and ordinary derived units. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-exact-square-comparison] with its exact functors $(r,s)=(U_{\overline X},U_Y)$ and $(H',H)=(p_*^{\mathrm W},p_*)$: both source hearts have K-injective resolutions, the forgetful functors are exact and $U_{\overline X}$ preserves K-injectives (Step 4), and $U_Yp_*^{\mathrm W}=p_*U_{\overline X}$ (Step 7). Let $d$ be its unique natural isomorphism $\beta$, so $d_{QI}\,U_Y\eta_I^{\mathrm W}=\eta_{UI}$ for every K-injective $I$. Both units are isomorphisms by the cited K-injective computation. Using their inverses to identify the targets with $Q(p_*UI)$ makes $d_{QI}$ the identity. Naturality along $s$ then identifies both units at $j_!^{\mathrm W}K$ with $Q(p_*Us)$. The native structure on $p_*^{\mathrm W}I$ is degreewise $p_*(\theta_I)a_{UI}$; ordinary derivation computes the Frobenius comparison on the same underlying K-injective $UI$. Indeed $P_{\overline X}UI\cong UI$ is also K-injective. Thus the two Frobenius arrows are literally $Q(p_*(\theta_I)a_{UI})$, and the identity comparison intertwines them.

source.place: Native refinement of the equivariance paragraph: the common K-injective representative and the identical lifted structure maps.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every derived morphism between the native K-injective resolutions is represented by a chain map uniquely up to homotopy. Both constructions send such a map $v:I\to I'$ to $Q(p_*Uv)$, so the identity comparisons commute with every derived morphism and with change of resolution. For shifts one may choose $I[n]$: it is K-injective because shifting an acyclic source remains acyclic, and the defining Hom group shifts back to a vanishing one. Both constructions use $p_*UI[n]=(p_*UI)[n]$ and the same shifted structure arrow, so $d$ respects shifts. Finally precompose $d$ with $j_!^{\mathrm W}$ and use the equality of Step 6, obtaining $c^0:U_YRp_*^{\mathrm W}j_!^{\mathrm W}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*j_!U_X$. This uses exactly the chosen ordered compactification construction of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Step 8 proves its asserted normalization and Frobenius compatibility. The argument applies on the ordinary ambient derived categories and requires no exceptional adjunction.
